feature: Customer Portal v2 -- the Security Plan (/portal-v2/security-plan), now reading REAL customer-scoped data from GET /api/portal/security-plan (routes/portal-security-plan.ts, requireRole CustomerUser, customerId from JWT) instead of the securityPlanData.ts design fixture. The plan of record is stored in four tables (portal_security_plans + _sections + _rows + _versions), seeded verbatim from the fixture (for the one testbed tenant only) by lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-21-portal-v2-security-plan.sql. Because that seed is a VERBATIM copy of the fixture, the on-screen text is identical whichever source rendered -- so this manifest's real-data proof is (1) a top-level apiTests GET that asserts the endpoint's own JSON, and (2) a uiStep on data-testid pv2-sp-source, which the page renders as one of FOUR honest dataState values (Git #1439): 'loading', 'live' (a real usable plan), 'no-plan' (read succeeded, this customer genuinely has none authored), 'error' (failed or malformed read). The design fixture is NEVER rendered in production any more -- see the #1439 note below. The met/partly/not-met tallies, the percentage and the section gap counts stay DERIVED on the client (securityPlanModel.ts) over whatever rows the endpoint returned.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the page. On a WebView2 with a PERSISTED session the two input steps (#email/#password) can fail because the session is already authed -- with only those two red and every page assertion green, that is a PASS for this feature.

THE LOGIN MUST BE A CustomerUser, NOT the Assessment TEST_PORTAL_* account. GET /api/portal/security-plan is requireRole('CustomerUser'); the Assessment-tier TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL 403s it, which now (Git #1439) sends pv2-sp-source to 'error', not a silent fixture. This manifest logs in with TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD -- a real CustomerUser testbed account (shanemccaw+buyassessment@outlook.com, users.id=39, tenant_id=1) whose customerId the seed row is keyed on. SHANE TO-DO: set TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD in BuildConsole Settings -> Test Environment Variables (point at users.id=39). This session ran it via a temp copy with those creds inlined.

SP-LIVE IS THE LOAD-BEARING REAL-DATA ASSERTION. pv2-sp-source renders the page's dataState; it reads 'live' only when GET /api/portal/security-plan returned a plan the wire could normalise. Git #1439: a customer with no plan authored now reads the honest 'no-plan', and a failed/malformed read reads 'error' -- the design fixture is never rendered for either case any more (it previously was, which is exactly what Shane's live testing caught -- 'Security Plan fake data' -- since the seed migration only seeds the one testbed tenant and every other real customer hit that silent fixture branch). Because the seed is verbatim-identical to the fixture, 'live' vs the fixture's own text is otherwise indistinguishable on screen, so this marker is critical.

THE DERIVED NUMBERS (SP4/SP5/SP6) ARE NOW DERIVED OVER REAL ROWS. round(20/39*100)=51%, 12 not met, 7 partly met, 20 met, 39 total -- these match the seed, which is a verbatim copy of the design content, so they read the same but are now computed by securityPlanModel.ts from the endpoint's rows. If the seed ever diverges from the design content, update these to the seed's numbers, not the design's.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/security-plan. App.tsx declares '/portal-v2/security-plan' BEFORE '/portal-v2/:pillar' so the param route cannot swallow it.

shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree -- a run against a build that predates the deploy of the route + wiring fails at SP-LIVE (source reads 'error', no endpoint reachable) or the apiTest, which is a not-deployed signal, not a page defect.

The requirement '-> Module' buttons and the version-history CR buttons navigate into other modules where those exist and are inert where the target page does not exist yet; this manifest asserts they RENDER, not that they navigate. The to/toLabel are stored verbatim from the seeded plan and the page keeps its own LIVE_ROUTES gate.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the CustomerUser testbed account; extract the bearer.
API1 -- the route exists, admits a CustomerUser, and returns this customer's own plan of record.
API2 -- the plan carries its numbered sections; take the first section's label to assert against the DOM.
API3 -- the first section's first requirement row, its real text pulled off the payload.
API4 -- the version history is real, newest first; take the top entry's CR code.

uiSteps.name: goto the real login URL (outer WouterRouter base = '/portal').
WAIT for the login form to hydrate before typing.
Primary login -- every assertion below needs a real CustomerUser session.
goto the Security Plan page on its slug-scoped route.
SP1 -- the page resolved to the Security Plan, not NotFound and not the param pillar route.

SP-LIVE (Git #1439) -- THE REAL-DATA ASSERTION. The page took the 'live' branch: pv2-sp-source reads 'live', which it does only once GET /api/portal/security-plan returned a plan the wire could normalise. A customer with no plan authored reads 'no-plan'; a failed/malformed read reads 'error' -- never a silent fixture.
SP2 -- the header names the tenant the ENDPOINT returned, and the environment.
SP3 -- the lead paragraph is the plan's own thesis, verbatim.
uiSteps.textContains: The authoritative record of how this tenant must be configured, monitored, governed and changed

uiSteps.name: SP4 -- the verdict is derived from the endpoint's gap and partial counts.
uiSteps.textContains: 12 requirements in this plan are not met, and 7 are only partly met.

uiSteps.name: SP5 -- the met percentage is derived (round(20/39*100) = 51%).
SP6 -- the count strip carries the four tallies.
SP7 -- the left rail lists the numbered sections.
SP8 -- the default selected section is the endpoint's first section.
SP9 -- its first requirement row carries the REAL requirement text the endpoint returned.
SP10 -- the version history renders under its own label, newest first, with the endpoint's top CR code.
SP11 -- select the PII governance section in the rail.
SP12 -- the section swaps: header and rows are now the PII requirements.
uiSteps.textContains: No PII reachable by an anonymous link

uiSteps.name: SP13 -- the 'Version history' label renders in the DOM.
SP14 -- from the Overview, clicking the Security Plan nav row navigates to the page. Go to Overview first.
SP15 -- click the Security Plan nav row.
SP16 -- it lands on the Security Plan page, still reading live.
